claim: llm-d-router maintainer Ezra Silvera stated the explicit design goal of the discovery abstraction: 'We aim to also support non k8s in the future so we need to keep the datalayer clean: we want K8s, file, Slurm, and Ray discovery all as plugins.'
stance_target: llm-d-router was deliberately architected to support pluggable non-Kubernetes discovery backends including file-based, Slurm, and Ray
quoted_support: We aim to also support non k8s in the future so we need to keep the datalayer clean: we want K8s, file, Slurm, and Ray discovery all as plugins. If discovery lives inside the datalayer, the datalayer gets contaminated with infrastructure-specific code (ctrl.Manager, fsnotify, etc.), which defeats the whole point of the abstraction.

claim: A custom discovery backend is enabled purely through configuration -- implementations of the EndpointDiscovery interface register in the router's plugin registry and are selected at runtime via the EndpointPickerConfig.discovery.pluginRef field, requiring no fork of the router core.
stance_target: concrete mechanism for adding a non-k8s backend to the router without forking it
scope_conditions: PR #908, merged May 3 2026 into llm-d-router main
quoted_support: Implementations must also implement fwkplugin.Plugin so they can be registered in the plugin registry and selected via EndpointPickerConfig.discovery.pluginRef.

claim: The discovery interface's core method, Start(ctx, notifier), is expected to enumerate all currently known endpoints via notifier.Upsert on startup and then block, continuing to watch for further changes until the context is cancelled or a fatal error occurs; the initial enumeration requirement was loosened during review from a hard requirement to a guideline.
stance_target: exact interface contract a custom discovery plugin implementation must satisfy
quoted_support: The requirement is here because without initial enumeration, the datastore starts empty and requests fail until the first event arrives. I will loosened from a hard requirement to a guideline

claim: The Notifier passed to a discovery plugin is not goroutine-safe, and plugin implementations must preserve event ordering themselves (e.g. an Upsert followed by a Delete for the same endpoint must arrive in that order) or the endpoint will be incorrectly left in the datastore.
stance_target: concurrency contract a custom plugin author must respect
quoted_support: Plugin implementations MUST preserve event order -- do not buffer or dispatch calls concurrently in a way that could reorder them. For example, an Upsert followed by a Delete for the same endpoint must arrive in that order, or the endpoint will be incorrectly left in the datastore.

claim: The discovery interface was intentionally placed under the datalayer package rather than as a peer component, because 'Discovery is upstream of the datalayer, not a peer -- the datalayer only activates per endpoint AFTER discovery creates it', with Discovery answering 'which endpoints exist?' and the datalayer answering 'what is the state of known endpoints?' (metrics, KV cache, queue depth).
stance_target: a custom non-k8s discovery plugin only needs to answer endpoint topology/existence; it can reuse the existing datalayer machinery for endpoint state/metrics if the backend exposes compatible telemetry
quoted_support: Discovery is upstream of the datalayer, not a peer, the datalayer only activates per endpoint AFTER discovery creates it... Discovery answers "which endpoints exist?". These are fundamentally different concerns -- topology management vs gather endpoint data.

claim: A reviewer flagged that using Kubernetes' types.NamespacedName as the endpoint identifier type in the Delete method is 'too k8s centric' and suggested an explicit backend-agnostic UniqueID instead; the author agreed this is a real gap affecting multiple places in the codebase but explicitly deferred fixing it as out of scope for this PR.
stance_target: the discovery interface is already fully backend-agnostic as of PR #908
scope_conditions: PR #908 review, Apr 30 2026 -- unresolved as of merge
quoted_support: I wonder if this is not too k8s centric and we should include an explicit UniqueID in the endpoint metadata? Not part of this PR. ... I agree. But it's wider than this instance. several other places using NamespacedName and we should switch to ID

claim: The DiscoveryPlugin interface was renamed to EndpointDiscovery during code review to avoid a redundant 'Plugin' suffix and to better convey directionality (outside world flowing inward to the datastore), distinguishing it from a hypothetical 'EndpointSource' concept that would flow the opposite direction (datastore events flowing outward to consumers).
stance_target: naming/API evolution of the discovery abstraction
quoted_support: EndpointManager implies it directly manages endpoints (deploy/remove them etc...). How about EndpointDiscovery ? ... EndpointSource vs EndpointDiscovery are opposite in direction... EndpointSource: datastore event --> outward --> consumers EndpointDiscovery: outside world --> inward --> datastore

claim: Follow-on work tracked alongside PR #908 includes issue #910 ('Refactor the Pod watching to fit the Discovery plugin', i.e. retrofitting the existing Kubernetes pod-watch mechanism into the new plugin interface) and issue #911 ('Implement a File discovery plugin'), plus a related closed PR #1007 ('Discovery Plugins: K8s and File-based Endpoint Discovery').
stance_target: immediate follow-up implementation work referencing this interface
quoted_support: Refactor the Pod watching to fit the Discovery plugin #910 ... Implement a File discovery plugin #911 ... Discovery Plugins: K8s and File-based Endpoint Discovery #1007
